the polynomial graph convolution is more expressive than the standard graph convolution, and that stacking multiple graph convolutional layers is not a viable solution for increasing the expressivity of the model, and that a single polynomial graph convolutional layer is enough to achieve the state of the art on several graph classification tasks.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we introduce a new convolutional layer, the Polynomial Graph Conv (PGC), that has a larger receptive field than the most common graph convolution operators.
the proposed PGC layer, with a single layer architecture, achieves better performance than a multi-layer architecture based on the most common convolution operator.
, in a GCN architecture, the number of GC layers is not a proxy for the network expressive power, and a single PGC is enough to reach the same performance.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the expressiveness of Graph Neural Network architectures is not limited by the size of the receptive field, but by the interactions among GC parameters in the stack.

, in order to exploit a larger receptive field in Graph Neural Networks, it is not sufficient to simply increase the size of the convolutional kernel, but it is necessary to consider the interactions between the different layers of the network.

the expressiveness of a graph convolution layer can be improved by considering wider receptive fields, and the most effective way to achieve that is not by stacking multiple non-linear convolutions, but by using a single PGC operator.
